bib.title: Trust Region Policy Optimization
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Lille, France, 2015. JMLR: W&CP volume 37

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; proofs in appendices A and B read but not re-derived.

question: How can a policy be updated with a guaranteed monotonic improvement in expected return, and can a practical approximation of that update train large nonlinear policies reliably?
hypothesis: Constraining the KL divergence between old and new policy gives a more robust step size than a fixed penalty coefficient and lets neural-network policies improve consistently with little tuning.
contributions: Prove that minimizing a surrogate objective with a KL (total variation) penalty guarantees policy improvement for general stochastic policies (Theorem 1, Eq. 9)
Approximate it by a hard average-KL trust-region constraint (Eq. 12), solved with conjugate gradient plus line search
Two sampling schemes: single path (model-free) and vine (needs state resets)
Show the same method learns swimming, hopping, walking gaits and Atari from pixels

method.summary: Surrogate objective L (Eq. 3) maximised under an average-KL constraint delta between old and new policy. Objective and constraint are estimated by Monte Carlo (single path or vine), the step direction comes from conjugate gradient on the Fisher matrix, and a backtracking line search enforces the constraint and objective improvement.
method.task: policy optimisation for reinforcement learning (MuJoCo locomotion, Atari)

datasets.name: Atari (ALE): Beam Rider, Breakout, Enduro, Pong, Q*bert, Seaquest, Space Invaders
datasets.preprocessing: following the protocol in Mnih et al (2013)

models.name: Locomotion policy (Gaussian MLP)
models.architecture: fully connected net to Gaussian mean, state-independent diagonal covariance via log std vector

models.name: Atari policy (CNN)
models.architecture: two conv layers, 16 channels, stride 2, one fully connected layer of 20 units, softmax over factored discrete actions

training.objective: maximise surrogate L_thetaold(theta) subject to mean KL(thetaold, theta) <= delta (Eq. 12/14)
training.optimizer: conjugate gradient (k=10 iterations) for direction A^-1 g, then backtracking line search with max step beta = sqrt(2 delta / s^T A s)
training.lr: none; step size is the KL bound delta = 0.01
training.batch_size: per iteration: locomotion 50K (swimmer) or 1M (hopper, walker) sim steps; Atari vine 400K, single path 100K sim steps
training.seq_len: single path: 1000 steps per path; vine rollout length 50 (swimmer), 100 (hopper, walker)
training.regularisation: KL trust region; Fisher-vector products computed on 10% subsample of data
training.wall_clock: Atari about 30 hrs for 500 iterations; vine 2/14/40 min and single path 5/35/100 (units as printed, 'computation time') for swimmer/hopper/walker
training.seeds: locomotion curves averaged over five runs; Atari run once per task

other.vine_sampling_dist_q: policy for continuous, uniform for Atari
other.natural_gradient_baseline: stepsize swept in factors of three, best by final performance
other.reward_function_not_restated: swimmer r = vx - 1e-5 ||u||^2; hopper same plus +1 non-terminal bonus

inference.samples: locomotion: five runs averaged; Atari: one run per game

metrics.name: learning curves of total reward / cost
metrics.definition: total reward (or cost) per policy iteration averaged over five runs

metrics.name: Atari game score
metrics.definition: score per game from a single run

eval.protocol: Locomotion: five random initialisations per algorithm. Atari: one run each, no error statistics ('time constraints').

results.claim: Policy improvement bound: expected return of the new policy is at least the surrogate minus a penalty proportional to max KL.
results.setup: Theorem 1 and Eq. 9; epsilon = max |A|, C = 4 eps gamma/(1-gamma)^2, using D_TV^2 <= D_KL
results.note: Equation text in extraction: eta(pi~) >= L_pi(pi~) - C D_KL^max(pi, pi~)

results.claim: Single path and vine TRPO solved all locomotion problems and gave the best solutions.
results.setup: cart-pole, swimmer, hopper, walker; five runs; vs CEM, CMA, natural gradient, empirical FIM, RWR
results.quote: Single path and vine TRPO solved all of the problems, yielding the best solutions.

results.claim: Natural gradient with a fixed penalty could not produce forward hopping or walking gaits, supporting the fixed-KL constraint.
results.setup: hopper and walker, stepsize swept in factors of three
results.quote: Natural gradient performed well on the two easier problems, but was unable to generate hopping and walking gaits that made forward progress.

limits: Monotonic improvement is proven only for the penalised form with the theory's large C; the practical algorithm uses a hard average-KL constraint and ignores advantage estimation error, so the guarantee does not hold in practice (authors say 'tends to give monotonic improvement').
Atari runs were single runs with no error statistics (Table 1 caption).
TRPO beats prior methods only on some Atari games; human performance exceeds it on most.
Vine needs resettable simulators and far more simulator calls.
Max-KL variant only tested on cart-pole.
Uses Monte Carlo Q-values, no learned value function/GAE; sample complexity high (1M sim steps per iteration for hopper, walker).
